verdicts.where: R-3, Basis and delta
verdicts.quote: The proposed default is automatic booking, disclosed at join, with first-joined priority among eligible entries.

verdicts.where: R-3 A, State and recovery, and Domain rules and open gaps
verdicts.quote: each newly bookable seat goes to the oldest eligible active entry for that occurrence. … The booking authority resolves concurrent joins in a deterministic commit order
verdicts.missing: Whether a membership tier or staff override can take precedence over join order.

verdicts.where: R-3, Domain rules and open gaps
verdicts.quote: Product and booking owners must confirm admission and allocation eligibility, definitive disqualification, membership and time conflicts
verdicts.missing: What happens to the other waitlist entry when the member is promoted into an overlapping class.

verdicts.where: R-2, Basis and delta and Domain rules and open gap
verdicts.quote: Preserve the rules for cancelling a confirmed booking. … including whether a newly confirmed booking can be cancelled
verdicts.missing: Whether declining or missing an automatic promotion counts as a late cancellation or no-show.

verdicts.where: R-3 A and C
verdicts.quote: even if the app was closed when the seat freed. … The booking authority reconciles a committed release after interruption without requiring member interaction.
verdicts.missing: How soon background allocation must complete after a cancellation frees a seat.

verdicts.where: R-3 A and Domain rules and open gaps
verdicts.quote: The promoted member sees **Booked** and ordinary booking details on return … outbound notifications are outside scope. Member status is available in-app.
verdicts.missing: The spec provides status on return but defines no promotion alert or recovery from a failed alert delivery.

verdicts.where: R-3 A–B
verdicts.quote: If multiple seats open, allocate in order up to available capacity or until no eligible entry remains. … Competing releases, direct bookings, repeated release signals and allocations cannot overbook or book any one member twice.

verdicts.where: R-3 B
verdicts.quote: While the outcome is pending the new requester sees availability being updated, with a refresh action. … Competing releases, direct bookings, repeated release signals and allocations cannot overbook or book any one member twice.

verdicts.where: R-3 D
verdicts.quote: Allocation cannot bypass a booking guard or impose a new automatic charge or commitment beyond established consent.
verdicts.missing: When an authorized payment is taken and what happens to the booking, entry and seat if payment fails.

verdicts.where: Non-functional requirements, Performance, freshness and quotas
verdicts.quote: Latency, throughput, queue size, availability, cost and runtime quotas are unresolved.
verdicts.missing: Whether the member waitlist has an admission cap, its value if capped, and what the next applicant sees at the limit.

verdicts.where: R-4 A and Domain rules and open gaps
verdicts.quote: Delayed release work cannot allocate on a closed occurrence or reopen an entry. … The schedule owner must establish cutoff, cancellation and schedule-change semantics
verdicts.missing: Whether final booking closure precedes class start and by how much.

verdicts.where: R-3 A and State and recovery; Behavior review, Concurrent capacity increase and direct booking
verdicts.quote: If multiple seats open, allocate in order up to available capacity or until no eligible entry remains. Remaining entries keep their order. … A capacity reduction follows existing policy for incumbent bookings.

verdicts.where: R-4 A
verdicts.quote: When the occurrence is cancelled, finally closes for booking or ends, waiting ends. Returning members can see the occurrence status and that their entries are inactive.

verdicts.where: R-5, Data lifecycle and runtime mapping
verdicts.quote: Booking authority owns shared membership and order across visits and devices. … Keep an entry active while waiting. Remove priority on leave, allocation, disqualification or closure.
verdicts.missing: Whether the entry records its join time and whether its position is stored or computed from the ordering data.

verdicts.where: R-4 A and R-5, Data lifecycle and runtime mapping
verdicts.quote: When the occurrence is cancelled, finally closes for booking or ends, waiting ends. … Retain only terminal information needed for status and recovery under approved retention, then remove it.
verdicts.missing: How long terminal entry information is retained after the class ends.

verdicts.where: R-5 A and Data lifecycle and runtime mapping
verdicts.quote: Denials reveal no other member's membership or identity. … Only the member's relevant status reaches their client.
verdicts.missing: Whether the member can see their own position in the queue.

verdicts.where: R-5 C
verdicts.quote: Authorized operators can correlate committed join, leave, allocation and closure outcomes and distinguish rejection, retries and outstanding recovery through existing coverage where adequate.
verdicts.missing: Which staff can view the waitlist, manually promote or remove a member, and see the promoted member and time for each allocation.

verdicts.where: R-1, Domain rules and open gaps
verdicts.quote: If the app cannot honor the disclosed allocation for a class type, the product owner must settle its join availability and wording before exposing the action for that type.
verdicts.missing: Whether there is a switch to disable the feature globally or configure it for individual classes or class types.

verdicts.where: Non-functional requirements, Integrity and recovery
verdicts.quote: The operations owner must confirm recovery obligations and any numeric completion deadline under R-3.
verdicts.missing: The maximum time from a committed cancellation to promotion of an eligible waiter.

verdicts.where: R-1, Basis and delta and B; R-5, Boundary contract and open gaps
verdicts.quote: Preserve ordinary booking when a seat is available under existing policy. … Joining leaves confirmed occupancy unchanged. … Changes affect only targeted entries and authorized bookings, preserving unrelated records.
